subject.title: fix(usage-bar): bound template override warning dedupe cache

question: When the invalid-template warning cache reaches 256 keys, should OpenClaw evict an old key and continue warning on new invalid overrides, or intentionally stop all new warnings until restart?
rationale: Both choices bound memory, but eviction preserves later diagnostics while the hard stop prevents warning churn; repository history establishes warnings as an operator-facing fallback signal but does not establish the saturation policy.

options.title: Evict Oldest Warning Key
options.body: Bound the set at 256 by deleting the oldest key before adding a new one, preserving warnings for later distinct invalid overrides.

options.title: Keep The Hard Stop
options.body: Retain permanent suppression after 256 keys, but add a focused saturation test and rationale showing that limiting diagnostic volume is intentional.

recommendation.title: Evict Oldest Warning Key
recommendation.body: Bound the set at 256 by deleting the oldest key before adding a new one, preserving warnings for later distinct invalid overrides.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced and merged the broken-template warning behavior whose saturation contract needs confirmation.
